textos.tag: OPEN 6 P.M. TO 6 A.M. · SECTOR NEON-07 · DIMENSION Ω
textos.titulo: Café Aurora — A Cyberpunk Café in Another Dimension
textos.descricao: Café Aurora, a fictional cyberpunk café: an example website by Linu Sites.
textos.hero_sub: We roast beans harvested from parallel realities. Every cup is a small quantum collapse — and your palate, the only constant.
textos.q1: I ordered a Quantum Espresso and started remembering a childhood I never had. Recommended. Back tomorrow — or yesterday.
textos.q2: The Plasma Latte glowed when I cried. It was awkward for both of us, but the flavor was flawless.
textos.sobre_h2: We were born from a short circuit between two worlds
textos.sobre_p1: In 2087, a barista named Aurora Vex spilled coffee on a warp reactor. The result wasn’t an explosion — it was an aroma.
textos.sobre_p2: The aroma opened a rift. On the other side was a city just like ours, but with lights that thought and rain that remembered. That’s where we found the beans we serve today.
textos.sobre_p3: Café Aurora is the only meeting point between the two cities, and it only exists at night: at 6 p.m., when the oven cools down, the rift opens again and the bakery counter becomes a café until 6 a.m.. Here, steam rises slowly and time agrees to pause for a few minutes — as long as you order a second cup.
textos.menu_lead: Six recipes calibrated for different brainwave frequencies. All served in self-regenerating cups.
textos.c1: Two simultaneous extractions in separate universes. You taste the average of both.
textos.c2: Milk steamed at 340 °C inside a magnetic field. It glows faintly when you stir.
textos.c3: Brewed for 72 hours in a sensory deprivation chamber. It syncs with your focus rhythm.
textos.c4: Leaves grown where there is no light. The taste arrives before the aroma — don’t ask how.
textos.c5: Caffeine-free. Made from condensed stardust and a little longing.
textos.c6: A triple shot with shards of orbital ice. The ice never melts — it just gives up.
textos.lab_lead: Adjust the parameters. The drink recalculates in real time — like everything here.
textos.q3: I only came in for coffee. I left with a theory about time and a cup that refuses to empty.
textos.cta_p: No booking needed. Just the courage to walk through the wrong door.
textos.foot_p: Interdimensional roasting since 2087. Beans ethically harvested in universes that gave their consent.
textos.addr3: Enter through the door that wasn’t there

textos.d_hero_sub: When the sun comes up, the rift closes and the oven comes on. We bake bread with flour milled in parallel realities: every slice comes out warm, crusty and just slightly out of time.
textos.d_sobre_h2: By day, the rift becomes an oven
textos.d_sobre_p1: Every morning, when our sun and Ω-11's rise together, the rift that Aurora Vex opened with coffee shrinks until it is the size of an oven door.
textos.d_sobre_p2: The heat that leaks through from the other side isn't wasted: it bakes bread. The first batch comes out at six, and the smell crosses both cities before any alarm clock goes off.
textos.d_sobre_p3: Aurora Bakery is the same place as the café, from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.. At the change of shift, the night baristas become bakers, the counter becomes a shop window and the neon rests until 6 p.m., when the rift opens again and the café comes back.
textos.d_menu_h2: Batches that don't wait for time to pass
textos.d_menu_lead: Six recipes that come out of the oven several times a day. All wrapped in paper that keeps the heat in for a few hours, or dimensions.
textos.d_c1: We fold the dough 2087 times, once for every year until the rift. Each bite crackles in a different layer of reality.
textos.d_c2: Proofed for 72 hours while floating, with nothing to pull it down. So light it comes tied to the plate.
textos.d_c3: Baked while making a full lap of the orbital oven. The crust sings when you squeeze it.
textos.d_c4: Filled with softly glowing custard and dusted with star sugar. Eat it before it decides to evaporate.
textos.d_c5: A ring donut whose crumb is always in shadow. Sugar on the outside; a little night on the inside.
textos.d_c6: Hot and cold at the same time until someone opens the bag. It always comes out hot.
textos.d_lab_lead: Pick the flour, the baking time and what goes on top. The crust browns while you decide.
textos.d_q1: I bought a croissant and found, between the layers, a note I'm going to write myself tomorrow. It was delicious.
textos.d_q2: The zero-gravity loaf floated up to the ceiling. I waited for it to come down before having breakfast. Back tomorrow.
textos.d_q3: I asked for one cheese bread and left with two: one from here and one from there. Both lovely and warm.
textos.d_cta_p: Come early: the first batch is gone before the sun has finished rising.
textos.d_foot_p: Interdimensional baking since 2087. Flour ethically milled in universes that gave their consent.

dep_partes: Debugging itself: depurar.js reads the page's CSS rules (document.styleSheets), the computed style (getComputedStyle) and the box (getBoundingClientRect) of the chosen part.

The opening screen: a <div> above everything, with the logo, the filling bar and the log lines. inicio.js shows it only on the first page of the session (sessionStorage) and script.js fills the bar in 0.9 s; it goes away with a tap, Esc, Enter or space.

The accessibility panel: a native <dialog> opened with showModal(), which keeps focus inside and closes with Esc. The choices become classes on <html> (a11y-contraste, a11y-links…) and are kept in localStorage; inicio.js applies them before painting, so the page does not flicker.
The panel button: created by recursos.js and pinned to the corner with position: fixed. The cut corners are a clip-path; the icon is a hexagon, also made with clip-path.

The language shortcut: it shows the code of the current language and opens the panel straight on the list. The address of each language comes from the <link rel="alternate" hreflang> tags in <head>, the same ones search engines read.
The Sign in link: recursos.js reads the session from localStorage and writes “Sign in” or “Hello, name”.

The sun and moon button: it swaps the Café (night) for the Bakery (day). It changes the data-modo attribute on <html>; the CSS redefines the color variables (block 17) and hides the .so-noite or .so-dia texts. Before that, the screen flickers like neon and the sun rises (or the moon sets).
The shift clock: every minute inicio.js checks the visitor's time and says what is open (bakery from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., café from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m.) and how long until the change.
The logo is just text and CSS: the dot (.brand__orb) is a circle with a radial gradient and a glow (box-shadow), pulsing in an animation (@keyframes pulse).

The three-line button (only on phone and tablet): script.js switches on the open class, which slides in the link drawer with transform: translateX(0). aria-expanded tells the screen reader whether it is open.
The menu links: the neon underline is an ::after that grows from 0 to 100% width. An IntersectionObserver lights up the link of the section in view.
The top bar: fixed (position: fixed), with a frosted-glass background (backdrop-filter: blur) over the animated background.

The photo of the front behind the title: WebP in two sizes (srcset and sizes), one at night and one by day, made as a pair in the same place. The one for the mode that is not showing is not downloaded.
The portal rings: three empty <i> elements, each a circle with a neon border (border-radius: 50%) spinning in a CSS animation at a different speed. Off screen, they stop to save the processor.

The halo: a conic gradient (conic-gradient) in the four colors, blurred with filter: blur(70px) and spinning slowly behind the title; the blur is done once and the layer only rotates (will-change: transform).

Magnetic button: script.js follows the pointer (pointermove) and pulls the button a few pixels with transform; when the pointer leaves, it goes back. On touch screens and with reduced motion, it stays still.
The neon button: a thin border in the accent color (--c), uppercase Orbitron text with wide letter spacing and a box-shadow glow on hover.
The numbers at the top: a flex list with the number in Orbitron and the smaller caption underneath.
The opening section: the title in Orbitron (a font served by the site itself), with a layered text-shadow glow. Whatever has .reveal appears on scroll, with an IntersectionObserver.
The scrolling strip: the text is there twice in a row and an animation moves the strip to translateX(-50%), so the end meets the beginning with no seam.

The menu search: an <input type="search"> inside role="search". recursos.js compares what you type with the name and the description, ignoring accents (normalize('NFD')), and announces the result with aria-live.
The filters: buttons with aria-pressed. script.js hides (hidden) the cards that do not match and counts how many are left.
The item details: a <details> with <summary>, which opens and closes without JavaScript and works with the keyboard.
The “+ Order”: script.js adds the item to the order (kept in localStorage) and updates the number on the Order button.

The menu card: an <article> with the photo (WebP, downloaded only when it gets close, loading="lazy"), label, price and the order button. On the phone the cards scroll sideways (scroll-snap), on the tablet there are 2 columns and on the computer 3 (CSS Grid).

The cup is drawn with CSS only: the body is a <div> with border-radius at the bottom, the handle is a pseudo-element with a border, the liquid (#liquid) changes height and color through script.js, and the steam is a set of animated strips. The extras switch on the classes com-1 to com-4.

The bread is CSS only too: a rounded shape (border-radius with eight values) and two gradients. The baking time darkens the crust (the --casca and --miolo variables) and the loaf rises a little (its height), all written by script.js; the toppings switch on the classes com-1 to com-4.
The builder: groups of buttons and a slider (<input type="range">). With each change, script.js puts together the name, the color, the price and the drawing.
The lab: two columns in CSS Grid (on the phone, one under the other), the builder on one side and the drawing on the other.
The gallery: the photos the site already has, the café's at night and the bakery's by day, each with alternative text and a caption (<figure> and <figcaption>), in a carousel.

The carousel, made by hand: the track is a strip with overflow-x and scroll-snap; the arrows and dots scroll to the slide (scrollTo). It moves on its own every 7 s and stops with the mouse over it, focus inside or “Stop animations”.
A review: <blockquote> with <q> (the browser adds the quotation marks) and a <footer> with who said it.
The Origin: text and the portal side by side in CSS Grid; the portal is a circle with a radial gradient and spinning rings.
The stamp card: ten dashed circles in a grid of five per row; each order sent stamps one (a magenta radial gradient), counted in localStorage.
The booking: a <form novalidate> that script.js checks as you type (name, people, day and a time within the shift). The error appears next to the field and is linked to it with aria-describedby.
Bookings: the form on one side, the stamp card and the bookings made on the other, kept in the browser.
The newsletter: script.js checks the email and answers in a message with role="status". It sends nothing anywhere: the Café is fictional.
The version switch: the same links in all five versions (plain CSS, Bootstrap, Tailwind, Bulma and Pico), with the current one marked with aria-current.
The footer: three columns in CSS Grid, which become two on medium screens and one on the phone.

The tuner: an <input type="range">. At night it changes the --desvio variable on <html>, and the four accent colors, hsl(calc(hue + var(--desvio)) …), all rotate at once. By day it becomes “Tune the light”: inicio.js writes the --luz-* variables with the time of the sun, from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., which slightly change the tone, the background and the photos.
The order: a <dialog> with the quantities, the total and the form. “Send on WhatsApp” opens the ready message (wa.me) with no number, because the Café is fictional.
The quiz: three questions in a <dialog>; script.js adds up the answers and picks the menu item that matches best.
The final call: the big title and two magnetic buttons.

The page content. Behind it, the background: a <canvas> (#bg) that script.js draws at 30 frames per second (20 on the phone), the perspective grid and particles at night, falling flour by day; on top, CSS layers (veil, noise and TV lines) with pointer-events: none, so they do not catch clicks.

The page: background var(--bg), text in Rajdhani and its own cursor (two <div> elements that follow the pointer, with mix-blend-mode: screen). Behind everything, the <canvas> of the animated background.
